title: Methodology for Gathering and Annotating Citing Documents of a Retraction
author: Ivan Heibi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqqumvww

steps.title: Select retracted article and retrieve metadata
steps.instruction: Use the Retraction Watch database (http://retractiondatabase.org/) to locate the retracted article of interest. Record the original DOI, the year of publication, and all years of retraction notices associated with the article. Also note the in‑text citation style used in the article, as this will be needed later.

steps.title: Gather citing entities and initial metadata
steps.instruction: Query the OpenCitations COCI dataset to obtain all works that cite the retracted article and collect their basic metadata (DOI, publication year, title, venue ID, venue title). Exclude any citing entity for which COCI does not return metadata. Create the main dataset **Cits_Dataset** with columns: doi_{var}, title_{var}, year_{var}, source_id_{var}, source_title_{var}.

substeps.instruction: Call the COCI “citations” operation (http://opencitations.net/index/coci/api/v1#/citations/) with the retracted article DOI to retrieve the list of citing DOIs.
For each citing DOI, call the COCI “metadata” operation (http://opencitations.net/index/coci/api/v1#/metadata/) to obtain the required fields.

Run the provided script to automate the above steps and write the output file (e.g., step_1_2.csv):
```
python3 method.py -s 1.2 -in "<retracted_DOI>"
python3 method.py -s 1.2 -in "<retracted_DOI>" -out path/to/dir
```

steps.title: Annotate citing entities with retraction status
steps.instruction: Add a column **is_retracted_{var}** to **Cits_Dataset** and fill it with “todo”. Then, for each citing DOI, check the Retraction Watch database to see whether the citing entity itself has been fully retracted. Replace “todo” with “yes” if it is retracted, otherwise “no”.

substeps.instruction:
Add the column and initialise it to “todo” using the script:
```
python3 method.py -s 2.1 -in "output/cits_dataset.csv"
```
Manually inspect each citing DOI in the Retraction Watch database (http://retractiondatabase.org/) and update the column accordingly.

steps.title: Classify venue IDs into subject area and category
steps.instruction: Separate ISSN and ISBN venue identifiers, map each to SCImago subject areas/categories (ISSN) or to LCC codes then to SCImago (ISBN), and merge the results back into **Cits_Dataset**.

substeps.instruction:
Create two index datasets containing the unique venue IDs:
```
python3 method.py -s 3.1 -in "example_data/cits_dataset.csv"
```

ISSN dataset (ISSN_Dataset): manually look up each ISSN on the SCImago Journal Rank site (https://www.scimagojr.com/). Record all subject areas and categories using the separators “;; ” between different areas and “; ” between categories within the same area. Store the results in columns **area_{var}** and **category_{var}**.

ISBN dataset (ISBN_Dataset): for each ISBN, obtain its Library of Congress Classification (LCC) code using the ISBNDB service (https://isbndb.com/) and the Classify service (http://classify.oclc.org/classify2/). Write the LCC code into column **lcc_{var}**.

Run the mapping script to convert LCC codes to SCImago areas and categories (automatically handling exact matches, category‑only matches, and flagging unmatched records as “todo_manual”):
```
python3 method.py -s 3.4 -in "example_data/cits_dataset.csv"
```
Manually resolve any records marked “todo_manual” by consulting the LCC index (http://www.loc.gov/catdir/cpso/lcco/) and entering the appropriate area and category.

Merge the annotated ISSN_Dataset and ISBN_Dataset back into the main **Cits_Dataset**, adding the columns **area_{var}** and **category_{var}**:
```
python3 method.py -s 3.5 -in "example_data/cits_dataset.csv"
```

steps.title: Add abstract and in‑text citation placeholders
steps.instruction: Extend **Cits_Dataset** with four new columns—**abstract_{var}**, **intext_citation.context_{var}**, **intext_citation.section_{var}**, **intext_citation.pointer_{var}**—and initialise each cell with the value “todo”.

substeps.instruction:
Run the script to add the placeholders:
```
python3 method.py -s 4.1 -in "example_data/cits_dataset.csv"
```

steps.title: Extract and fill abstract and citation details
steps.instruction: For each citing entity that has an accessible full‑text, retrieve the abstract and locate every in‑text citation of the retracted article. Populate the placeholder columns with the extracted information; remove any citing entity lacking a full‑text from the dataset.

substeps.instruction: Manually download or otherwise obtain the full‑text of each citing article (skip pay‑walled items and delete those records).
Copy the full abstract into **abstract_{var}**; if no abstract exists, leave the cell empty.
Identify the exact in‑text citation pointer(s) (e.g., “Heibi(2019)”) and write the value into **intext_citation.pointer_{var}** (one value per citing entity).

For each pointer, extract the surrounding context: the sentence containing the pointer plus the preceding and following sentences. Apply special rules for pointers appearing in titles, table cells, first/last sentences of sections. Concatenate multiple contexts with the separator “;; ” and store in **intext_citation.context_{var}**.

Determine the section where each pointer occurs. Assign a type from {abstract, introduction, background, results, method, conclusion, discussion} when the section title matches; otherwise record the position (first section, middle section, final section) and, if needed, the exact title in brackets. Separate multiple sections with “;; ” and separate type from title with “; ”. Store the result in **intext_citation.section_{var}**.

steps.title: Add citation intent, sentiment, and retraction mention fields
steps.instruction: Extend **Cits_Dataset** with three new columns—**intext_citation.intent_{var}**, **intext_citation.sentiment_{var}**, **intext_citation.ret_mention_{var}**—and set every cell to “todo”.

substeps.instruction:
Run the script to create the columns:
```
python3 method.py -s 5.1 -in "example_data/cits_dataset.csv"
```

steps.title: Manually assign intent, sentiment, and retraction flags
steps.instruction: For each citing entity, read the previously filled **intext_citation.context_{var}** and apply the following rules to replace the “todo” values:

substeps.instruction: Intent: Use the CiTO ontology (https://sparontologies.github.io/cito) to select a single citation‑intent property that best matches the context. If multiple candidates exist, compute the priority score (sum of x‑ and y‑axis values plus cell value) and choose the one with the lowest score. Separate multiple intents with “;; ”.

Sentiment: Assign “positive” if the retracted article is cited as a valid prior work, “negative” if it is criticized or deemed invalid, and “neutral” if no judgment is expressed. Separate multiple sentiments with “;; ”.
Retraction mention: Set to “yes” only if the word “retract” (or any derivative) appears explicitly in any citation context; otherwise set to “no”.
